name: note-open-close
title: A note opened from the list and closed with Done (#322)
description: Design 5.5. Desktop: the note's text comes from the direction of the list, 18 px (snap); let go, its words fade where they were (140 ms, exit) and the row's highlight fades (150 ms). Android: the note grows out of its card (440 ms, enter; its text rises 14 px behind it, 380 ms from 60 ms) and shrinks back into it (340 ms, standard), its words riding with it onto the card's, fading as a whole into the card from 140 ms (200 ms, standard), so that it lands as the card (#322).

movements.name: open
movements.description: The second note in the list is pressed.

movements.name: close
movements.description: Done: Esc on the desktop, which has no ✓ (design 7.14); ⌄ on Android. Back to the list.

handsOver.because: design 5.5: the note becomes its card; its words ride with the page onto the card's, the whole page fades into the card from 140 ms, and it lands as the card (#322)

mirrors.because: design 5.5: on Android the note grows out of its card (440 ms, enter) and shrinks back into it (340 ms, standard); on the desktop a note let go only fades, by design, so nothing there is meant to mirror

movements.name: open-again
movements.description: The second note is opened again, for the next movement.

movements.name: done-then-bar
movements.description: Done, and at once the bar, for the next thought (design 5.8, checklist A31). No wait between the two taps: the driver's own round trips on the emulator already put the second about 130 ms after the first, and a further 120 ms had put it at about 350 ms, after the 340 ms close, when the page had gone and the keyboard (on a boot that shows one) was going and moving the bar 312 px down from where it was found. The page on its way out lets the tap through, and a new page opens out of the bar. It is then let go empty.

movements.name: open-once-more
movements.description: The second note is opened again, for the next movement.

movements.name: done-then-card
movements.description: Done, and at once another card (design 5.8), with no wait between the taps, as above: the tap goes through the page on its way out, and the third note grows out of its own card, afresh, not out of the second's. It is then let go.
